questions.stem: CSF from a febrile college student with neck stiffness and a petechial rash shows the Gram stain pictured: red, kidney bean-shaped paired cocci inside neutrophils. Which organism is most likely?

explanation.summary: N. meningitidis is a gram-negative (red) diplococcus described as kidney bean-shaped, often seen within neutrophils. S. pneumoniae is a gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococcus, H. influenzae is a gram-negative coccobacillus, and S. agalactiae/S. aureus are gram-positive.
explanation.whyCorrect: N. meningitidis is a gram-negative (red) diplococcus described as kidney bean-shaped, often seen within neutrophils. S. pneumoniae is a gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococcus, H. influenzae is a gram-negative coccobacillus, and S. agalactiae/S. aureus are gram-positive.

questions.stem: The diagram compares two outer-membrane glycolipids. The right-hand form, lacking the outer repeating polysaccharide chain, is characteristic of which organism in this brick?

explanation.summary: The LPS of most gram-negative bacteria contains lipid A, a core polysaccharide, and an O antigen. N. meningitidis LPS lacks the O antigen, producing the shorter lipooligosaccharide (LOS), which acts as an endotoxin that can trigger a cytokine storm. Gram-positive organisms have no outer membrane LPS at all.
explanation.whyCorrect: The LPS of most gram-negative bacteria contains lipid A, a core polysaccharide, and an O antigen. N. meningitidis LPS lacks the O antigen, producing the shorter lipooligosaccharide (LOS), which acts as an endotoxin that can trigger a cytokine storm. Gram-positive organisms have no outer membrane LPS at all.

questions.stem: A Gram stain from a child with acute epiglottitis shows the small pink organisms pictured among neutrophils. The organism grows on chocolate agar but not on plain blood agar. Which organism is most likely?

explanation.summary: H. influenzae is a small, nonmotile, gram-negative coccobacillus that requires factors X (hematin) and V (NAD), so it grows on chocolate agar but not on blood agar. It causes epiglottitis, meningitis, otitis media, and pneumonia.
explanation.whyCorrect: H. influenzae is a small, nonmotile, gram-negative coccobacillus that requires factors X (hematin) and V (NAD), so it grows on chocolate agar but not on blood agar. It causes epiglottitis, meningitis, otitis media, and pneumonia.

questions.stem: H. influenzae is grown on the brown medium shown, made by heating blood agar to lyse the red cells. Why does this medium support its growth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lysed RBCs supply factors X (hematin) and V (NAD)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bile salts select for the organism

choices.label: D
choices.text: High salt selects for the organism

explanation.summary: Chocolate agar is blood agar heated to lyse the red cells, releasing factors X and V that fastidious H. influenzae requires. Thayer-Martin agar is chocolate agar with added antibiotics and antifungals, used to select Neisseria from non-sterile sites.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chocolate agar is blood agar heated to lyse the red cells, releasing factors X and V that fastidious H. influenzae requires. Thayer-Martin agar is chocolate agar with added antibiotics and antifungals, used to select Neisseria from non-sterile sites.

questions.stem: On this blood agar plate, H. influenzae colonies grow only near the S. aureus streak. What explains this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: S. aureus catalase removes toxic hydrogen peroxide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Beta-hemolysis by S. aureus releases factors X and V

choices.label: C
choices.text: S. aureus ferments mannitol, acidifying the agar

choices.label: D
choices.text: S. aureus coagulase produces a fibrin scaffold

explanation.summary: This is the satellite phenomenon. H. influenzae cannot lyse RBCs to obtain X (hematin) and V (NAD) factors, so it cannot grow on plain blood agar, but it grows next to beta-hemolytic bacteria such as S. aureus, which lyse red cells and release those factors.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is the satellite phenomenon. H. influenzae cannot lyse RBCs to obtain X (hematin) and V (NAD) factors, so it cannot grow on plain blood agar, but it grows next to beta-hemolytic bacteria such as S. aureus, which lyse red cells and release those factors.

questions.stem: A Gram stain from a deep, foul-smelling wound shows the large organisms pictured. The isolate grows only anaerobically and is catalase negative. Which genus is most likely?

explanation.summary: Clostridia are large gram-positive (purple), obligately anaerobic rods that are catalase and oxidase negative. Staphylococci and streptococci are gram-positive cocci, and Haemophilus and Neisseria are gram-negative.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clostridia are large gram-positive (purple), obligately anaerobic rods that are catalase and oxidase negative. Staphylococci and streptococci are gram-positive cocci, and Haemophilus and Neisseria are gram-negative.

questions.stem: A wound isolate from a patient with crepitus and muscle necrosis grows anaerobically on blood agar with the double zone of hemolysis around each colony shown. Which organism is most likely?

explanation.summary: C. perfringens produces a characteristic double ring of beta-hemolysis on blood agar, reflecting its multiple toxins. It causes gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis), driven mainly by alpha toxin, a lecithinase.
explanation.whyCorrect: C. perfringens produces a characteristic double ring of beta-hemolysis on blood agar, reflecting its multiple toxins. It causes gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis), driven mainly by alpha toxin, a lecithinase.

questions.stem: A stained smear shows rods with round terminal swellings, giving the drumstick appearance pictured. Which genus forms these structures?

explanation.summary: Clostridia are spore-forming gram-positive rods, and their spores have a drumstick appearance. Spores let clostridia survive adverse conditions, including oxygen exposure. None of the cocci or gram-negative organisms listed form spores.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clostridia are spore-forming gram-positive rods, and their spores have a drumstick appearance. Spores let clostridia survive adverse conditions, including oxygen exposure. None of the cocci or gram-negative organisms listed form spores.

questions.stem: A man who stepped on a rusty nail develops a fixed grimace (left) and severe arching back spasms (right), as shown. The responsible toxin blocks release of which neurotransmitters?

choices.label: B
choices.text: GABA and glycine from inhibitory interneurons

explanation.summary: This is tetanus (risus sardonicus and opisthotonos). C. tetani tetanospasmin cleaves SNARE proteins in inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells), preventing GABA and glycine release and causing spastic paralysis. Botulinum toxin, by contrast, blocks acetylcholine release at the NMJ.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is tetanus (risus sardonicus and opisthotonos). C. tetani tetanospasmin cleaves SNARE proteins in inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells), preventing GABA and glycine release and causing spastic paralysis. Botulinum toxin, by contrast, blocks acetylcholine release at the NMJ.

questions.stem: A teen develops drooping eyelids and dilated pupils (shown), followed by descending weakness, after eating home-canned vegetables. Which organism is responsible?

explanation.summary: Botulism: preformed C. botulinum toxin inhibits acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, producing a descending flaccid paralysis that starts with the cranial nerves (ptosis, dilated pupils) and can progress to respiratory failure. It is associated with home-canned foods.
explanation.whyCorrect: Botulism: preformed C. botulinum toxin inhibits acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, producing a descending flaccid paralysis that starts with the cranial nerves (ptosis, dilated pupils) and can progress to respiratory failure. It is associated with home-canned foods.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old fed honey develops constipation followed by acute, generalized hypotonia, appearing limp as shown. What is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Infant botulism (floppy baby syndrome) occurs in infants under 1 year whose immature GI tract lets ingested C. botulinum spores germinate and colonize the bowel. It presents with constipation and then generalized hypotonia. Treatment is botulism immune globulin and supportive (often ventilatory) care, not antibiotics.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infant botulism (floppy baby syndrome) occurs in infants under 1 year whose immature GI tract lets ingested C. botulinum spores germinate and colonize the bowel. It presents with constipation and then generalized hypotonia. Treatment is botulism immune globulin and supportive (often ventilatory) care, not antibiotics.

questions.stem: A 73-year-old man develops vomiting and diarrhea after drinking fresh, unpasteurized farm milk. The micrograph shows the causative organism, a gram-positive facultative intracellular rod, inside a host cell. Which growth property helps this organism persist in refrigerated foods?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Growth at refrigerator temperatures (cold enrichment at 4 C)

explanation.summary: Listeria monocytogenes is a gram-positive, facultative intracellular rod. It grows across a broad range of temperatures, pH and salt, including 4 C ('cold enrichment'; 'Cool Mint Listermean'), so it persists in refrigerated foods such as unpasteurized milk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Listeria monocytogenes is a gram-positive, facultative intracellular rod. It grows across a broad range of temperatures, pH and salt, including 4 C ('cold enrichment'; 'Cool Mint Listermean'), so it persists in refrigerated foods such as unpasteurized milk.

questions.stem: Several days after starting an antibiotic, a patient develops the widespread blotchy red rash shown on the back. Which adverse effect of antibiotic therapy does this represent?

explanation.summary: Antibiotics can cause allergic reactions ranging from mild cutaneous reactions, like this rash, to anaphylaxis. Penicillin allergy is the one most often reported, although many such patients are not truly allergic when properly evaluated. A careful medication and allergy history is part of antibiotic selection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiotics can cause allergic reactions ranging from mild cutaneous reactions, like this rash, to anaphylaxis. Penicillin allergy is the one most often reported, although many such patients are not truly allergic when properly evaluated. A careful medication and allergy history is part of antibiotic selection.

questions.stem: An adult finishing a course of broad-spectrum antibiotics develops the white oral plaques shown. By what mechanism did the antibiotics predispose to this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They killed normal bacterial flora, allowing Candida to overgrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: They caused an allergic mucosal reaction

explanation.summary: This is oral thrush (oral candidiasis). Antibiotics disrupt the normal bacterial flora that competes with Candida, so the fungus overgrows, producing thrush or vulvovaginal candidiasis. This is one reason to limit antibiotic use to clinically indicated situations.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is oral thrush (oral candidiasis). Antibiotics disrupt the normal bacterial flora that competes with Candida, so the fungus overgrows, producing thrush or vulvovaginal candidiasis. This is one reason to limit antibiotic use to clinically indicated situations.
